title: Plus Worksheet Benefit and Plus Excluded Total: Computation
content:
**GAP Waiver Addenda, GAP Waiver Plus 150 claim worksheet.** The claim is the latest claim reported on the addendum: the claim with the latest reporting date, or, where two were reported on that date, the one recorded first on the addendum.

## The benefit

The Plus worksheet benefit is the starting balance the claim shows, less the loan-to-value excess, less the Plus excluded total, less the primary insurer's net settlement. It is never below 0.00, never above the plan's largest benefit for one loss, and rounded half-up to the cent.

- **Loan-to-value excess.** The amount by which the contract's amount financed exceeds the plan's highest covered loan-to-value percent of the vehicle's book value at origination, times the starting balance the claim shows divided by the amount financed. It is 0.00 when the amount financed is within that limit.
- **Net settlement.** The primary insurer's actual cash value the claim shows, less the primary deductible the claim shows.

## The Plus excluded total

The Plus excluded total is the sum of six parts, added without rounding and then rounded half-up to the cent.

| Part | Amount |
|---|---|
| Past-due | the installments it counts, which are all the installments treated as past due, times the installment amount it uses, which is the contract's scheduled payment, less the partial installment credit the contract carries, never below 0.00 |
| Fee | the fees due the contract carries less the late charges assessed on installments that fell due after the date of loss, never below 0.00 |
| Deferral | the deferred installments it counts, which are all the installments deferred by every extension the contract records, times the installment amount it uses, which is the contract's scheduled payment |
| Placed-premium | every force-placed premium the insurance tracking record added to the contract balance |
| Add-on | the price of the service contract financed on the contract times the calendar days from the date of loss to its expiration date divided by the calendar days from its enrollment date to its expiration date, rounded half-up to the cent, when it was enrolled on or before the date of loss and expires after it; 0.00 when there is no such service contract |
| Uncovered-deductible | the primary deductible the claim shows less the part of it the plan covers, which is that deductible up to the plan's deductible reimbursement maximum, never below 0.00 |

**Installments treated as past due.** These are the installments still unpaid that fell due on or before the date of loss. They are counted from the contract's next due date, one a month, through the date of loss: the whole months from the next due date to the date of loss, plus one. None are counted when the next due date is after the date of loss.

**Whole months.** Whole months from one date to a later one are the difference in calendar months between them, less one when the later date's day of the month is below the earlier date's.

**Installments that fell due after the date of loss.** These are the installments whose due date is fewer whole months before today than a set figure. That figure is the whole months from the contract's next due date to today, less the whole months from the next due date to the date of loss.

## Plans this computation governs

- On a GAP Waiver Plus 150 claim, the excluded amounts the benefit deducts are the Plus excluded total. Salvage retained by the borrower and prior-damage deductions, which the claim records do not carry, stay excluded at the claim decision as the settlement documents state them.
- The Plus benefit is reduced by this loan-to-value excess, figured on the starting balance the claim shows, in place of the portion above the plan's covered loan-to-value percent.
- The Plus benefit deducts this net settlement and adds no deductible covered. The part of the deductible above the plan's deductible reimbursement maximum is among the excluded amounts.
- A GAP Waiver Premier 150 claim is itemized under the Premier excluded total, reduced by the Premier worksheet benefit's own loan-to-value excess, and worked under the Premier worksheet benefit.
- A claim on any other plan is still reduced by every excluded amount in the plan's definitions, with salvage retained by the borrower excluded at the plan's salvage basis. It is also reduced by the portion above the covered loan-to-value percent, amortized in the same proportion as the scheduled balance, and it deducts the actual cash value and adds the deductible covered.

### Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

The hypothetical claim shows a starting balance of 15200.00, an actual cash value of 9100.00 and a deductible of 680.00, under a plan covering deductibles up to 500.00. The contract shows 21000.00 financed on a book value of 13000.00, with a covered percent of 150. The excluded parts are:

- past-due: one installment of 410.00 treated as past due, with no partial credit, giving 410.00;
- fee: 60.00;
- deferral: one installment of 410.00;
- placed-premium and add-on: none;
- uncovered deductible: 680.00 less 500.00, which is 180.00.

The Plus excluded total is 1060.00. The excess is 1500.00 times 15200.00 divided by 21000.00, which is 1085.714. The net settlement is 8420.00. The benefit is 15200.00 less 1085.714, less 1060.00, less 8420.00, which is 4634.29.
